messages:
helen_sales: LumenCare POC: they want Redwood Private inside their transit VPC, must retain original client source IP for audit, and they run TLS-inspect in a DMZ. Also asked: rough cost comparison between static EIP-per-AZ vs shared NAT. Need a 1-page + checklist for NetOps.

diego_se: Short: doable. Key point: if traffic is SNATed by a TGW/NAT you'll lose the true client IP. Options: PrivateLink ENIs (avoid SNAT), internal NLB with static EIP mapping, PROXY protocol from their DMZ proxy, or 1:1 SNAT (EIP per host). Tradeoffs: cost, HA behavior, and app changes for PROXY header.

samir_netops: Quick topology q: are they using Direct Connect -> TGW (likely hairpin) or VPN into spokes? If service traffic can route to PrivateLink ENIs we can avoid the centralized NAT. Also watch MTU with IPsec/encap (recommend PMTU ~1400).

nora_sec: TLS-inspect note: acceptable if customer retains certificate keys. We recommend terminating mTLS inside their VPC (Redwood connector supports mTLS + customer KMS). I'll draft SQ wording: TLS min 1.2, prefer 1.3, allowed ciphers, and audit log retention options.

diego_se: Pasteable allowlist snippet for their firewall/team: 

```
# Egress -> Redwood Private
Allow TCP 443 -> *.redwood-private.<region>
Allow UDP 123 -> 0.0.0.0/0  # NTP
# Optional inbound health checks
Allow TCP 443 <- <redwood-health-ips>
```

FQDN allowlist preferred; we publish IP ranges when needed.

samir_netops: Src-IP options quick summary: 1) NLB+static EIP = stable external source (map flows), 2) DMZ proxy + PROXY/X-Forwarded-For = true client IP if app supports, 3) 1:1 SNAT EIP = costly but direct. Note: ALB needs proxy protocol to preserve src IP.

helen_sales: Pricing ask: can we give a ballpark delta for per-EIP vs NAT for the customer?

diego_se: Ballpark guidance: managed per-EIP add-on is a Private-deploy option, usually billed monthly per-EIP (order of magnitude: tens to low-hundreds USD per EIP/month depending on region/contract) plus egress. Shared NAT approach is lower infra cost but provides no sticky per-customer source IP guarantee. I'll confirm exact numbers with finance and add to the onboarding doc.

onboard-bot: [onboard-bot] Connectivity checklist updated: https://redwood.internal/onboard/lumencare/connectivity

samir_netops: Ops callouts: set TCP keepalive <60s for long streams, document idle timeouts for proxies, and flag multi-region sticky egress as a POC risk.

diego_se: Action items: Diego -> 1-page decision matrix (PrivateLink vs TGW vs peering) with src-IP tradeoffs and sample PROXY header. Samir -> short ops note (MTU/keepalive). Nora -> security questionnaire text. Helen -> confirm LumenCare's preference and whether they accept PROXY headers or require per-EIP.

helen_sales: I'll run the checklist with LumenCare tomorrow and share the one-pager. Thanks team :thumbsup:
